name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Colonial-era hill station at about 1,500 m with pine forests, lakes, markets, and a pleasant climate, serving as the main base for exploring the Khasi Hills.
facts: Named after the deity Lei Shyllong
Former capital of undivided Assam until 1972
Hub for education and Khasi culture

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at approximately 1,965 m, about 10 km from Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, waterfalls, and distant plains. Sacred to the Khasi people with a sanctum for the deity U Lei Shillong.
facts: Requires photo ID for entry near radar station
Popular for sunrise and sunset views
About 10 km south of Shillong city

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong in Upper Shillong, East Khasi Hills. Known locally as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Easily accessible with steps to different levels, surrounded by ferns and greenery.
facts: Named after a former elephant-shaped rock
Original Khasi name means three-step waterfall

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, near Sohra (Cherrapunji) in East Khasi Hills. Plunges from the plateau edge into a turquoise pool. Associated with a local Khasi legend of Ka Likai.
facts: Named after the legend of Ka Likai

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic hill station and former wettest place on Earth, headquarters of Sohra subdivision in East Khasi Hills. Famous for heavy rainfall, waterfalls, caves, living root bridges, and dramatic limestone cliffs overlooking the Bangladesh plains.
facts: Once recorded as the wettest place on Earth
Base for Nohkalikai, Mawsmai Cave, and root bridges

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village in East Khasi Hills near the India-Bangladesh border, famous as one of Asia's cleanest villages. Features living root bridges, balancing rock, bamboo viewpoints, and well-maintained streets with community tourism.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia in 2003 by Discover India
Home to a living root bridge and balancing rock

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic double-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, East Khasi Hills, near Sohra. Formed by guiding aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees over generations by Khasi people. Requires a trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna.
facts: Part of UNESCO tentative list for living root bridges
Trek from Tyrna village near Sohra

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint in East Khasi Hills near Smit, about 25 km from Shillong. Offers sweeping views of deep green valleys and ridges, with a steep path of stone steps descending to Rasong village below.
facts: Steep descent of nearly 3,000 steps to lower village
Popular for photography and short treks

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) near Mawphlang village in East Khasi Hills, protected by Khasi traditions for centuries. Dense temperate rainforest with rare flora, orchids, and cultural significance; visitors must not remove anything.
facts: Protected by traditional beliefs for centuries
Home to rare plants and orchids

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Limestone show cave near Sohra in East Khasi Hills, with lit passages, stalactites, and stalagmites. About 150 m accessible length, one of the easier caves for visitors in the region.
facts: Lit show cave suitable for most visitors

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall near Mawsmai village in East Khasi Hills, also called Seven Sisters Falls. Drops about 315 m in multiple streams over limestone cliffs, spectacular in monsoon with views toward the plains.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures (Museum)
description: Major museum in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, traditions, and lifestyles of indigenous peoples of Northeast India. One of the largest museums of its kind in the region with extensive ethnographic collections.
facts: Also known as Don Bosco Museum

name: Jowai Town
description: District headquarters of West Jaintia Hills and cultural centre of the Pnar (Jaintia) people. Hill town at about 1,380 m elevation on a plateau surrounded by the Myntdu River, serving as the main base for exploring waterfalls, lakes, and heritage sites in the district.
facts: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district (formed 2012)

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning turquoise-blue waterfall in Amlarem subdivision, cradled in a forested valley. Features a natural swimming pool at the base; one of the most photogenic falls in Meghalaya with short trek access.
facts: About 30 km from Jowai, ~90 km from Shillong

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of megalithic monoliths (menhirs and dolmens) in Meghalaya, erected between 1500 and 1835 AD by Jaintia kings and clans. Tallest menhir about 8 m; former summer capital area of the Jaintia kingdom.
facts: About 25 km from Jowai, 65 km from Shillong
Tallest menhir ~8 metres erected by Mar Phalyngki

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: Ancient 600-year-old Durga Temple at Nartiang, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Historically associated with the Jaintia kings; features unique local traditions.

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake (Pung Sajar Nangli) on NH-6 near Mukhla village. According to legend, dug by followers of chieftain Sajar Nangli using bow ends to commemorate an exodus.
facts: About 8-10 km from Jowai on NH-6
Also known as Sajar Nangli Lake

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tier waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai road. Accessible via an arch bridge over paddy fields with a short walk; often compared to Elephant Falls but taller.

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town on the India-Bangladesh frontier famous for the crystal-clear Umngot River where boats appear to float in air. Features the 1932 British suspension bridge and boating; major photography and adventure hub.
facts: About 95 km from Shillong, near Bangladesh border
Umngot River renowned for exceptional clarity

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Village on the Umngot River near Dawki offering quieter boating, camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, and riverside stays. Less crowded alternative to main Dawki ghat with adventure activities.
facts: A few km from Dawki on Umngot River

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Scenic riverside spot on the Myntdu River near Jowai, meaning 'golden flower'. Historical site linked to freedom fighter U Kiang Nangbah; popular local picnic and angling area with suspension bridge.
facts: Site associated with U Kiang Nangbah
Popular local picnic and angling spot

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park about 8 km from Jowai featuring sacred grove, viewpoints over Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu River, walking trails, and picnic areas. Developed under district tourism projects.
facts: Views of Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered secluded waterfall near Shkentalang/Jarain with turquoise plunge pool. Requires moderate trek through forest; offbeat nature spot with camping options nearby.
facts: About 20-22 km from Jowai near Shkentalang

name: Thlu Muwi
description: Historic megalithic stone bridge over the Muwi stream, about 16 km from Jowai on the Dawki road. Built by Jaintia warriors for kings travelling to Nartiang; adjacent to Muwi Waterfalls.
facts: 16 km from Jowai on Jowai-Dawki road
Stone bridge built for Jaintia kings
